:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: Without using a calculator, find the exact value of $\cos^2\left( 22.5^\circ\right) - \sin^2\left( 22.5^\circ\right).$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
First, let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x = \cos 2x
$$

Substituting $x={22.5^\circ}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\cos }^{2}⁡({22.5}^{∘})-{\sin }^{2}⁡({22.5}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot {22.5}^{∘}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡{45}^{∘} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

:step/content.:tutorial/content:
Recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(x+y) = \cos x \cos y - \sin x \sin y
$$

  

Substituting $y={\color{blue}x}$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x,\end{aligned}
$$

which simplifies to

$$
\cos 2x = \cos^2 {x}  - \sin^2 {x}.
$$

This is called the **double-angle formula for cosine**.

:step/content.:tutorial/content:
It's possible to write the double angle formula for cosine in two alternative forms.

From the Pythagorean identity $\sin^2{x}+\cos^2{x}=1,$ we obtain $\cos^2{x}=1-\sin^2{x}.$
Substituting this into the double-angle formula for cosine, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x & ={\cos }^{2}⁡x-{\sin }^{2}⁡x \\  & =(1-{\sin }^{2}⁡x)-{\sin }^{2}⁡x \\  & =1-2{\sin }^{2}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives an alternative form of the double-angle formula for cosine. We'll restate it below:

$$
\cos{2x} =1 - 2\sin^2{x}
$$

Similarly, from the same Pythagorean identity, we obtain that $\sin^2{x}=1-\cos^2{x}.$ Substituting into the double-angle formula for cosine, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x & ={\cos }^{2}⁡x-{\sin }^{2}⁡x \\  & ={\cos }^{2}⁡x-(1-{\cos }^{2}⁡x) \\  & =2{\cos }^{2}⁡x-1.\end{aligned}
$$

This is another alternative form of the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\cos{2x} =2\cos^2{x}-1
$$
